title: Double Smash Burgers
subtitle: Crispy edges, melty cheese, crew-approved

steps.title: Mix sauce & prep
steps.instruction: Stir mayo, mustard, and ketchup into a quick burger sauce. Slice onions paper-thin. Split buns. Form beef into loose balls (about 3 oz each) — don't pack tight or burgers steam instead of crisp.

steps.title: Smash on the flat-top
steps.instruction: Heat griddle or cast iron over high until smoking. Ball down, smash immediately with a stiff spatula into a thin patty. Season with salt. Cook 2 minutes until edges lace and brown. Flip, add cheese, stack if doing doubles. Toast buns in leftover fat.

steps.title: Stack the burgers
steps.instruction: Bottom bun → sauce → pickles → patty with melted cheese → onions → top bun. Serve within 2 minutes — smash burgers lose their crisp edge fast. Run a sheet-tray line, not individual plating.

steps.title: Hold the batch
steps.instruction: Keep finished burgers on a rack in a 200°F oven up to 8 minutes. Wipe the griddle between batches so fat does not burn the next round.

proTips: Smash once per side — re-smashing after crust forms tears the lace.
American cheese melts faster than cheddar; use it for that diner drape.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Toast buns in batches and hold in a warm pan — soggy buns kill the line.
Keep cheese slices under a dome so they melt fast when patties come off the griddle.
Line up Double Smash Burgers on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Store components separate — assemble fresh; buns go soggy overnight.
